(AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster) Carolyn Kaster/AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster Former New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady , rocker Jon Bon Jovi, and other star-studded guests attended a Manhattan fundraiser Wednesday that raised $32 million for Robert Kraft’s Blue Square Alliance Against Hate, the group said. 
 The group said it was the largest single-night fundraising total in its history. 
 Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots, launched the alliance as the Foundation to Combat Antisemitism in 2019 and it was rebranded last year as the Blue Square Alliance Against Hate. 
 The alliance works to “inspire Americans to stand up to Jewish hate and all hate,” its website states. 
 The group also documented the festivities, held at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City, on its social media channels. 
 “Joined by passionate allies including Tom Brady, Michael Rubin, and Jon Bon Jovi, we sent a clear message that antisemitism and hate has no place in our communities,” the alliance wrote on Facebook. 
 The alliance said it also honored Brian Moynihan, CEO of Bank of America, “for his continuing commitment towards this works. Together, our voices are louder and stronger in the fight against hate.” 
 This story will be updated when more information is released.
